reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses HEA coating properties but not particle size effects on thickness. E2 describes mechanical milling size evolution, irrelevant to thermal spray deposition efficiency. E3 notes oxidation of small particles but does not demonstrate that inert gas shielding or larger particles reduce oxidation or improve thickness. No evidence links larger feedstock to higher deposition efficiency or validates the inert gas mechanism.
premises: Larger particles (50–60 μm) increase deposition efficiency and coating thickness relative to 15–45 μm feedstock.
Inert gas shielding reduces in-flight oxidation during thermal spray of HEAs.
Reduced oxidation preserves coating integrity and microstructure.
FeCoNiCrAl HEA bond coats can be deposited by thermal spray with acceptable properties.
